performers: The Tudor Consort; Alastair Carey, director
question: How can passing a figure between voices suggest a bird’s movement?
intro: Monteverdi’s five-part madrigal turns a bird’s song into an argument about love. Follow the exchanges between voices rather than looking for one permanent soloist.

sections.label: Opening exchanges
sections.mNote: short moving figures circulate among the upper voices

sections.label: Middle span
sections.mNote: more sustained writing contrasts with the opening movement

sections.label: Final intensification
sections.mNote: moving figures and sustained lower notes lead towards the close

cues.title: The bird has several voices
cues.text: The score begins with the upper three parts, leaving tenor and bass silent until later. Follow the quick figures shared between the upper lines: the madrigal suggests a bird’s activity through vocal movement, not through an added instrument.
cues.evidence: Daniel Van Gilst’s CC0 score, p. 1, shows the initial upper trio and the later lower-part entries. This is an opening-span observation; no exact second is assigned to the tenor or bass entrance. https://ks15.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/b/b7/IMSLP561996-PMLP525417-Monteverdi,_Claudio_-_Quel_augellin_che_canta_(5vx).pdf

cues.title: Guarini’s bird speaks of love
cues.text: The poem comes from Giovanni Battista Guarini’s Il pastor fido. A bird moves between trees, and its song becomes an imagined declaration of love, answered by its mate. Monteverdi adapts the passage rather than setting the whole dramatic scene.
cues.evidence: LiederNet identifies Act I, scene 1, lines 175–186 and gives the differences in Monteverdi’s sung text. The imagery is described without assigning a word to this timestamp. https://www.lieder.net/lieder/get_text.html?RF=0&TextId=7068

cues.title: Motion against longer notes
cues.text: In the middle stretch, compare the longer held notes with the smaller movements around them. The choir can reduce the sense of activity without becoming a single sustained chord; independent phrases still pass through the texture.
cues.evidence: The score’s middle pages contrast longer lower-part values with moving upper lines. The report shows reduced onset density and lower recorded level around 0:55–1:15 relative to the opening crest. This supports a broad contrast, not individual note alignment.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: An Ordizia concert, not 2010
cues.text: This performance comes from the Tudor Consort’s concert in Ordizia on 2 November 2005, directed by Alastair Carey. The 2010 date on the download page belongs to its online release, not the singing in the church.
cues.evidence: FMA’s track description names Ordizia and Carey; the album liner notes date that concert to Wednesday 2 November 2005. FMA labels 19 August 2010 “Released”. https://freemusicarchive.org/music/The_Tudor_Consort/Live_in_Concert

transitions.title: Longer values temper the opening movement
transitions.how: The five-part writing places more sustained notes against the active figures, changing the balance between motion and held sound. This is a vocal contrast: no continuo or orchestral colour is introduced. The passage moves away from the opening’s concentration of quick upper-voice figures while the individual lines retain their independence.
transitions.evidence: The score’s middle pages show longer lower-voice values and more sustained ensemble writing. The report marks a boundary at 0:40, followed by lower levels at 0:45 and 0:55–1:15. The marker is a broad grouping, not a timed textual entrance.

transitions.title: Renewed motion gathers the final phrase
transitions.how: The ending combines moving upper lines with longer supporting notes below. Repeated fragments extend the final phrase, and the recorded sound grows towards another crest before settling. The same five vocal parts supply the added weight; a fuller passage does not mean that an instrumental ensemble has joined.
transitions.evidence: The last page of the score shows running figures, repeated fragments and sustained lower-part notes. The measured boundary at 1:26 precedes rising level through 1:30–1:40 and a final fall after 1:45. No exact sung syllable or cadence time is asserted.

source.title: Monteverdi, Quel augellin che canta, ed. Daniel Van Gilst (2019), CC0

timeline.note: Voices alone: the score begins with an upper trio and later uses all five parts. The display groups the choir rather than timing each part’s rests.

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: The Tudor Consort (vocal ensemble), Alastair Carey (director)
fields.note: The track description and Carey’s album notes agree. Five written parts do not establish five individual singers, and no instrumental players are credited.

fields.label: Work version
fields.note: The opened score supplies two soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts, without instruments. Neither the exact edition used by the choir nor its performance transposition is established.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: The track names the Ordizia concert; the album’s first-person liner notes explicitly date it to Wednesday 2 November 2005. The 19 August 2010 date on FMA and Commons is an online release, not the recording session.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: The track and album notes name the venue. The later Rome concert and 2006 New Zealand recording described elsewhere in the same album notes belong to different tracks.

fields.label: Label
fields.note: The album was prepared for the Tudor Consort’s twentieth anniversary, but no original imprint is named. FMA and Commons are access repositories.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.note: No commercial catalogue number is supplied.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: The notes refer to a disc but supply no matrix, mastering identifier or take number.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.value: Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer; Commons import by ComputerHotline
fields.note: Hurd is explicitly credited at album level. The Commons uploader is not presented as the original engineer.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.note: The 2005 concert date, 2010 FMA release and 11 April 2020 Commons upload do not establish a mastering or transfer date.

fields.label: Processing

The actual FMA recording page supplies independent evidence.
